Mountainous

/MOWN-tuh-nus/ · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Mountainous means having many mountains, or relating to high, rugged terrain.

Mountainous means having many mountains, or relating to high, rugged terrain. Three quarters of the country is mountainous, and only the coastal strip is flat enough to farm.

Worked Example

A rail company costs two routes of equal length between the same two cities. The northern route crosses flat farmland and needs nine bridges, no tunnels, and a maximum gradient of one percent. The southern route climbs three passes above 2,000 metres, requires fourteen tunnels and thirty-one viaducts, and closes for snow most winters. The engineers price the southern line at four times the northern one, because the country it crosses is mountainous.

Three passes above 2,000 metres, fourteen tunnels, and regular winter closures describe country built of high peaks rather than gentle ground, which is what mountainous means.

How Mountainous Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

rugged

rugged: rough, steep, and hard to cross

alpine

alpine: belonging to high mountains

Antonyms

flat

flat: without significant variation in height

lowland

lowland: lying low, near sea level

How Strong Is It? — hilly → alpine → mountainous

hilly vs. mountainous

hilly vs. mountainous: Hilly ground rises and falls but never reaches true peaks, while mountainous country does.

alpine vs. mountainous

alpine vs. mountainous: Alpine is narrower than mountainous, pointing at the high, treeless zone near the summits rather than at the whole mountain landscape.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — mountain-

Root — mountain-: mountain (Latin mons, montis)

Suffix — -ous

Suffix — -ous: full of; having

Put it together

Put it together: Latin mons, mountain, came into English through Old French montaigne, and adding -ous ('full of') gives land that is full of mountains. The same mons climbs through surmount, which is to get over an obstacle, and paramount, which once meant 'up above' and now means highest in importance.

Use the root in a new word: paramount

Use the root in a new word: paramount: Something paramount stands above everything else, from the same Latin mons ('mountain') that makes a country mountainous.

Word Choice

plain descriptive

Mountainous describes the land itself and, by extension, anything of mountain size, as in a mountainous pile of laundry. It names one kind of terrain rather than the general subject of terrain, since the arrangement of a region's surface features as a whole is its topography, taught elsewhere in this unit.
